1.1  Cabinet Approves Rs 9,585 Crore Scheme for Replacement of Old Trucks & Buses in Delhi-NCR to Promote Cleaner Mobilityp.6
Exam Hints:
  • What: Approval for scheme to replace old trucks and buses in Delhi-NCR
  • By Whom: Union Cabinet chaired by PM Narendra Modi
  • Financial outlay: Rs 9,585 crore for 2 years
  • Target vehicles: 1.91 lakh trucks, 16,329 buses (total 2.07 lakh)
  • Funding: NCRPB (MoHUA)
  • Implementation: MoRTH, MoPNG, in collaboration with Haryana, Rajasthan & UP
  • Key Benefits: 5% interest subvention for 5 yearsMonthly fuel vouchers up to Rs.4,800Registration fee waivers & tax concessions by States8% ex-showroom discount by OEMsEmpowered Committee: Chaired by the Cabinet Secretary, Dr. T. V. Somanathan.
About Delhi-NCR Vehicle Replacement Scheme:
  • Outlay: The scheme has a total outlay of Rs. 9,585 crore, including Rs. 5,041 crore in Central support and Rs. 1,601 crore in State tax concessions, with a two-year enrolment period, five-year Central incentives, and a target of replacing 2.07 lakh vehicles (1.91 lakh trucks and 16,329 buses).
  • Significance: The scheme directly targets high-emission vehicles, promotes scientific scrappage and circular economy practices, strengthens the National Vehicle Scrappage Policy, (NVSP) 2021, enables digital governance, serves as a model for nationwide fleet renewal programmes, and contributes to India’s Net Zero 2070 commitment.
Scheme Benefits:
  • State Government Incentives: Offers registration fee waivers, up to 100% motor vehicle tax concession for new vehicles, 50% tax concession for used BS-VI vehicles for ten years, and waiver of pending liabilities.
  • OEM Support: Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs) provide an 8% ex-showroom discount on eligible vehicles.

Exam Hints:
  • What: Approval of Rs 10,000 crore ATF Price Stabilization Fund
  • Approved by: Union Cabinet, chaired by PM Narendra Modi
  • Purpose: To support Indian Airlines which are affected by rising global fuel
  • Duration: Up to 3 years, subject to annual review
  • Key Advantage: Interest-free advances to OMCs via MoPNG
Background:
  • The newly approved mechanism is expected to provide enhanced stability and predictability in ATF pricing for Indian airlines, enabling better operational and financial planning.
Key Details:
  • Coverage: The budgetary support will be available to all interested scheduled Indian carriers for both domestic and international operations.
  • Duration: As per the Government of India (GoI), the newly approved arrangement will remain in force up to 36 months (3 years), subject to annual review or until the support amount is fully recovered, whichever is earlier.
  • Key Benefits: The arrangement is expected to support continued air connectivity to remote, regional, Tier-II and Tier-III cities, including airports operationalised under the Ude Desh ka Aam Nagrik (UDAN) scheme.This budgetary support will protect the 77 lakh jobs dependent on the aviation sector.
About Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas (MoPNG):
  • Union Minister: Hardeep Singh Puri (Rajya Sabha- Uttar Pradesh, UP) Minister of State (MoS)- Suresh Gopi (Constituency- Thrissur, Kerala)

Exam Hints:

1.7  Union Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan Launches Month-Long ‘Khet Bachao Abhiyan’ Campaign in MPp.14
Exam Hints:
  • What: Launch of ‘Khet Bachao Abhiyan’ campaign
  • By whom: Union Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan, MoAFW
  • Where: Ramsiya village in Raisen, MP
  • Duration: June 1 to 30, 2026
  • Objective: Promote sustainable farming, soil conservation, and climate-resilient agriculture
  • Implementation Partners: Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs), ICAR teams, Panchayats
  • Important Schemes Linked: KCC, PM-KISAN, Pulses & Oilseeds Mission, Oil Palm Mission, Cotton Mission.
Background:
  • The month-long initiative commenced on June 1, 2026, and will continue until June 30, 2026.
About Khet Bachao Abhiyan:
  • Objective: This campaign promotes soil-test–based balanced nutrition, green manures, organic and bio-fertilisers, and Integrated Nutrient Management (INM) through field demonstrations.
Operation Framework:
  • Coordination: Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs) designated as key coordinators, with over 1,600 teams formed, including 500 teams in high fertiliser-use districts and 1,150+ multidisciplinary teams from ICAR (Indian Council of Agricultural Research) and KVKs.These teams will ensure scientific outreach and effective field-level implementation.
  • Integration: The campaign takes a holistic approach beyond fertiliser management by linking farmers to Kisan Credit Card (KCC), PM-KISAN (Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi), Pulses and Oilseeds Mission, Oil Palm and Cotton Missions, and soil health and water conservation initiatives.It ensures region-specific advisories and inclusion of left-out beneficiaries.

1.15  Kerala Launches India’s First Judiciary-Integrated Wildlife Offence System ‘HAWK’p.22
Exam Hints:
  • What: HAWK (Hostile Activity Watch Kernel) System launched
  • Launched By: Kerala
  • Significance: India’s first fully digitised and judiciary-integrated wildlife offence management system
  • Type: Cloud-based ERP platform for wildlife crime management
  • Purpose: Strengthens investigation, prosecution, intelligence gathering & monitoring of wildlife crimes and Illegal Wildlife Trade
  • Collaboration: Wildlife Trust of India, NTT Data.
About HAWK System:
  • Evolution: HAWK was conceptualised in 2015 during Operation Shikar following the Malayattoor elephant poaching case in Kerala.
  • Integration: It links forest records with the District Court Management System through an Application Programming Interface (API), making Kerala the first state in India with a judiciary-integrated wildlife offence management system.
  • Collaboration: HAWK was developed by the Kerala Forest Department in collaboration with the Wildlife Trust of India (WTI) and Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Data Corporation (NTT Data).
  • Access: The system provides digital dashboards for officials from Divisional Forest Officer (DFO) to Chief Conservator of Forests (CCF).
  • Other Launches: Kerala Forest Department launched a 24×7 Forest Call Centre and an online Solar Fence Monitoring Portal to strengthen digital forest governance and monitoring across the state.

1.16  Union Minister Amit Shah Launches LPMS ‘VINIMAY’ to Digitise Cargo & Passenger Movement at Land Portsp.23
Exam Hints:
  • What: Launch of LPMS – ‘Vinimay’
  • By Whom: Union Minister Amit Shah, MHA
  • Where: New Delhi, Delhi
  • Objective: Modernise & digitise land port operations, facilitate trade
  • Developed by: LPAI
  • Coverage: 15 operational land port, 11 more port planned over 2–3 years
  • Integration: ICEGATE, CBIC, BSF, DGFT, UIDAI, ULIP
  • Key Features: Single Electronic Window (SEW), Automatic Number Plate Recognition (ANPR), online payments, slot booking, and tracking.
About LPMS VINIMAY:
  • Development: It was developed by LPAI under MHA.
  • Benefits: The system eliminates about 90% of paperwork, reduces truck waiting time by 40–60%, cuts gate processing time by 22–35%, and enhances efficiency, transparency, security, and inter-agency coordination in cross-border trade and passenger movement.
  • Expansion: 11 additional land ports are planned to become operational over the next 2–3 years, expanding India’s border trade infrastructure.
  • Trade: Trade through land ports increased from Rs.5,000 crore in 2014 to Rs.83,000 crore in 2026, reflecting a sixteen-fold rise in cross-border commerce.
About Land Ports Authority of India (LPAI):
  • statutory body established under the Land Ports Authority of India Act, 2010, functioning under the Department of Border Management (DBM), Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA), to develop and manage border infrastructure and Integrated Check Posts (ICPs).
  • Chairman: Jayant Singh
  • Headquarters: New Delhi, Delhi
  • Established: 2012

  • Applicability: CSR obligations apply to companies that, in the immediately preceding financial year, have a net worth of Rs.500 crore or more, turnover of Rs.1,000 crore or more, or net profit of Rs.5 crore or more, with the Corporate Laws Amendment Bill, 2026 proposing to increase the net profit threshold to Rs.10 crore.

  • Key Benefits: Duty-Free Access: 99.38% of Oman’s tariff lines covering 98.08% of India’s exportsIndia’s Tariff Liberalisation: 77.79% tariff lines covering 94.81% of imports from OmanBeneficiary Sectors: Gems & Jewellery, Textiles, Leather, Marine Products, Engineering Goods, PharmaceuticalsServices Market Access: 127 service sub-sectorsMobility Provisions: Business Visitors (90 days), Independent Professionals (180 days), ICTs (up to 4 years) and others.
About India-Oman CEPA:
  • Key Target: Through CEPA, overall GoI has set the ambitious target of achieving 2 trillion of exports in next 5 years (i.e. by 2031).
Key Features:
  • Duty-Free Export: CEPA offers 99.38% of its tariff lines which includes 98.08% of India’s exports, making it one of the most comprehensive market access outcomes secured by India in the Gulf region.Earlier, under the MFN regime, only 15.33% of India’s exports entered Oman duty-free.
  • Liberalised Tariffs on Imports from Oman: On the other hand, the GoI offers liberalised tariffs on 77.79% of its total tariff lines, which covers 94.81% of what India imports from Oman.
  • Mobility: Under CEPA, business visitors can now stay in Oman for a maximum of 90 days; Independent professionals (up to 180 days); Intra-Corporate Transferees (ICTs) (up to 4 years).
India’s FTA Progress:
  • Key Progress: In the last 3.5 years, India has signed 9 Free Trade Agreements (FTAs), covering 38 developed nations and securing preferential access for goods and services across nearly 2/3rd of global target.

  • What: Letter of Request (LoR) for 114 Rafale fighter jet
  • Who: Ministry of Defence (MoD), Government of India
  • Partner Country: France
  • Value: Rs. 3.25 lakh crore
  • Aircraft: Rafale multirole fighter jets
  • Beneficiary: Indian Air Force (IAF)
  • Mode: Government-to-Government (G2G) deal
Background:
  • Under the proposed deal, Out of the 114 Rafale jets, around 94 aircraft are proposed to be manufactured in India by French manufacturer Dassault Aviation in partnership with an Indian company.
Key Details of Agreement:
  • Objective: India’s Multi-Role Fighter Aircraft (MRFA) programme aims to procure 114 fighter jets to address the IAF capability gap, as its squadron strength has declined to 29 squadrons against the sanctioned requirement of 42.5 squadrons.
  • Procurement: IAF ordered 36 Rafales in 2016, while the Indian Navy ordered 26 Rafale Marine jets in 2025.
  • Technology Transfer: This deal marks the first-ever production of Rafale aircraft outside France, with around 50% indigenous content.
About Rafale Fighter Aircraft:
  • Overview: Rafale is a 4.5-generation multirole fighter aircraft fly up to Mach 1.8 (~1,912 km/h) and a combat radius over 1,850 km without refueling is developed by Dassault Aviation.

Background:
  • The initiative aims to enable end-to-end tracking of foodgrain movement, prevent bag recycling, and improve transparency in procurement, storage, and distribution.
About QR Tagging Initiative:
  • Background: The initiative follows successful QR-tagging pilots for rice in AP (December 2025–January 2026) and wheat in Punjab (April–May 2026).

About Ramsar Convention on Wetlands:
  • Background: international treaty for wetland conservation and sustainable use, was adopted in 1971 in Ramsar, Iran, and came into force in 1975.
  • Aim: It provides a framework for the conservation and sustainable use of wetlands across its 172-member countries, including India (which acceded to the treaty on February 01, 1982).
  • Total Ramsar Sites in the World: As of June 2026, total number of Ramsar sites in the world is 2,595 (Surha Taal as 2,595th such site globally).

1.43  Government announces Measures to Deepen the G-Sec market and Facilitate greater FPIp.48
Exam Hints:
  • What: MoF introduced series of reforms to increase FPI participation in G-secs Taxation Changes
  • Old: FII and FPI were taxed 30% for STC and 12.5% for LTC
  • Now: FPI/FII taxed nil for interest income and capital gains earned from G-sec
  • Effective from: 1 April 2026
  • BIS: IT exemption provided for BIS FAR Expansion
  • Securities included: 15, 30, 40-year G-secs and SGrBs
  • Limits removed: Short-term investment limit, Concentration limit; and Security-wise investment limit. PROI Liberalisation
  • PROI: permitted to invest in equity instruments of listed Indian companies
  • Limit increased: 10% in any company, overall limit – 24%
Changes in Taxation:
  • Previously: Previously, Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs), including SEBI-registered Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs), were taxed under Section 210 of the Income-tax Act, 2025.Any income earned from investments in Government Securities (G-Secs) was subject to tax.Short-term capital gains (STC) were taxed at 30% and Long-term capital (LTC) gains were taxed at 12.5%
Expansion of FAR:
  • FAR Expanded: The government has expanded the list of securities eligible under FAR, to enhance participation by FPIs in G-Sec.New issuances of 15-year Government Securities;New issuances of 30-year Government Securities;New issuances of 40-year Government Securities; andSovereign Green Bonds (SGrBs) issued in FAR-eligible tenors.
PROI Liberalisation:
  • Investment limit increased: The investment limit will be increased for an individual PROI under this scheme from 5% to 10% in any company, with an overall investment limit for all individual PROIs to 24%, from the current 10%.

1.57  India & Japan Adopt Rules for JCM under Paris Agreement to Boost Climate Cooperationp.65
Exam Hints:
  • What Launched: JCM Rules adopted on 8 June 2026.
  • Partners: India and Japan.
  • Basis: Article 6.2 of the Paris Agreement.
  • Mechanism: Joint Crediting Mechanism (JCM).
  • Focus: Emission reduction and carbon credit generation.
  • Structure: Joint Committee and project approval framework.
  • Outcome: Climate action and low-carbon technology deployment
Background:
  • The move strengthens India-Japan cooperation in climate action, Greenhouse Gas (GHG) emission reduction, carbon markets, and sustainable development.
About the JCM Under Paris Agreement:
  • Background: Paris Agreement (2015) under the UNFCCC aims to combat climate change.
  • Provision: Under Article 6.2 of the Paris Agreement, countries can cooperate through the transfer of internationally recognized carbon credits to achieve climate goals.
  • Framework: India and Japan adopted the JCM Rules on 8 June 2026, following the Memorandum of Cooperation (MoC) signed in 2025, to operationalise bilateral emission-reduction projects.
  • Mechanism: JCM is a bilateral carbon market mechanism that supports emission-reduction projects, low-carbon technologies, and carbon credit generation while contributing to the NDCs of India and Japan.
  • Benefits: JCM will promote investment, technology transfer, capacity-building, decarbonisation, and Greenhouse Gas (GHG) emission reduction in India.
  • Chairperson: Simon Steill
  • Established: 1994

2.5  Ladakh LG Vinai Kumar Saxena Approves Constitution of SHAN Conservation Societyp.78
Exam Hints:
  • What: Constitution of the Snow Leopard and High-Altitude Nature (SHAN) Conservation Society
  • Who: Approved by Ladakh LG Vinai Kumar Saxena
  • Purpose: Scientific conservation of biodiversity, wildlife protection, and promotion of eco-tourism
  • Focus Areas: Snow leopard habitat conservation, biodiversity management, human-wildlife conflict mitigation, and sustainable livelihoods
Background:
  • Society, under the Department of Environment and Forests, Ladakh, will serve as a dedicated institutional mechanism for wildlife conservation, biodiversity management, and community-led environmental stewardship across Ladakh.
Key details of Approval:
  • Objective: Society serves as a multi-stakeholder platform to conserve Ladakh’s alpine fauna and flora, wetlands, and cold desert ecosystems through eco-development in snow leopard habitats and eco-tourism promotion.
  • Significance: The initiative highlights the conservation of the snow leopard, the State Animal of Ladakh and a keystone species of the Trans-Himalayan ecosystem, revered as the “Ghost of the Mountains” essential for maintaining mountain habitats, prey populations, and regional watersheds, and an indicator of ecosystem health.According to the 2024 Snow Leopard Population Assessment in India, there are 718 snow leopards in the country, including 477 in Ladakh.

Background:
  • The penalty was imposed by the RBI under Section 47A(1)(c) read with Sections 46(4)(i) and 51(1) of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949.
Identified Regulatory Lapses:
  • Inspection: The penalty was imposed following the Statutory Inspection for Supervisory Evaluation (ISE 2025), which audited Canara Bank’s operations as of March 31, 2025.

6.5  RBI Releases Amendment Directions easing Bank Lending Norms for REITs and InvITsp.112
Exam Hints:

  • Purpose: Eased lending to REITs and InvITs

  • Operational Assets: 80% and cash generating for more than 1 year
  • Effective from: October 1, 2026

Lending Framework Norms:
  • Operational Assets: For REITs, lending will be restricted to listed trusts where at least 80% of assets comprise cash-generating properties that operational for more than one year.Similarly, banks may lend only to listed InvITs with at least 80% of assets invested in completed and revenue-generating infrastructure projects with positive cash flows for one plus year.
  • Effective From: These Directions shall come into force from October 1, 2026, or an earlier date when adopted by a bank in entirety.
  • Risk Weight Norms: Risk weights have been revised, with REIT exposures set at 100% (or 125% if classified as capital market exposure), while InvIT exposures will attract corporate lending risk weights.RBI said these exposures will eventually shift to a capital charge framework starting April 1, 2027.

Exam Hints:
  • What: Master Directions on Authorisation of PSO
  • Released by: RBI
  • Objective: Covers eligibility criteria, authorisation, perpetual validity of licences, voluntary surrender, and cooling-off requirements.

PSO Licensing Framework:
  • Authorisation: Under Section 4 of the PSS Act, 2007, no person, other than the RBI, can commence or operate a payment system without obtaining prior authorisation from the RBI.Therefore, any entity intending to establish or operate a payment system must apply for authorisation under the PSS Act, 2007.
  • Validity Period: New Payment System Operators (PSO) authorisations will be perpetually valid, while existing operators may receive perpetual validity at renewal subject to regulatory compliance.Non-compliant PSO may receive 1 year renewals until deficiencies are addressed.
About PSS Act, 2007:
  • Board: RBI shall exercise the powers, perform the functions and discharge the duties conferred on it under the PSS Act, 2007 through a Board to be known as the “Payments Regulatory Board”.
  • Regulations: Under the PSS Act, 2007, two Regulations made by the RBI, namely, the Payment and Settlement Systems (PSS) Regulations, 2008 and the Payments Regulatory Board (PRB) Regulations, 2025.

  • Applicable to: The directions apply for Commercial Banks (CBs), Small Finance Banks (SFB), Regional Rural Banks (RRBs), and Rural Co-operative Banks (RCBs).
  • Crop Season Standardized: This refers to the period from the raising of crops to their harvesting and marketing.Crop seasons shall be standardised at 12 months for short duration crops and 18 months for long duration crops.
  • Marginal Farmers Limit: Marginal farmers shall be eligible for a flexible credit limit of Rs 10,000 to Rs 50,000, as Flexi KCC.
  • Note: Marginal farmer means a farmer with landholding of up to one hectare.

  • The revised directions come into effect from June 24, 2026.
Key Revisions:
  • New Criteria: Upper Layer shall consist of NBFCs having asset size of Rs 1,00,000 Cr and above per the latest audited balance sheet for the Financial Year (FY).
  • Concentration Norms: Government-owned NBFCs will now be subject to the same concentration risk limits applicable to their regulatory layer (Base, Middle, or Upper).The exposure limit to a single counterparty is 25% of Tier 1 capital and to a group of connected counterparties is 40% of Tier 1 capital.
  • Infrastructure Finance Company (IFC): Directions increase the exposure limit for an NBFC-IFC (Upper Layer) to a group of connected counterparties from 40% to 45% of its Tier 1 capital.They permit an additional exposure of up to 20% of Tier 1 capital beyond the prescribed limit.

Exam Hints:
  • What: Introduction of Revised Trading Framework for ETFs
  • Who: SEBI
  • Effective From: September 01, 2026
  • Key Changes: ▪ Dynamic Price Bands for ETFs; ▪ New Methodology to Determine ETFs Base Price; ▪ Pre-Open Call Auction for Commodity ETFs; ▪ Equity and Debt ETFs: 10%; band expansion limit (20%) ▪ Commodity ETFs: ±6%, band expansion limit (3%).
Background:
  • As per SEBI’s circular, the new trading rules for ETFs will come into effect from September 1, 2026.
Key Changes:
  • Equity and Debt ETFs: Replacing the existing fixed 20% price band based on the Net Asset Value (NAV) for equity ETFs and debt ETFs, the revised framework introduced dynamic price band (excluding overnight and liquid ETFs) with initial limit of 10%, which can later be expanded up to 20% after a cooling-off period.The price band will be expanded by 5% increments if prices hit the upper threshold during the trading session.
  • Pre-Open Call Auction: The revised norms introduced a pre-open call auction mechanism specifically for commodity ETFs to enhance better price discovery, while domestic ETFs trade only during Indian market hours.

About Lifecycle Funds:
  • Overview: Lifecycle funds, called target-date funds, are mutual fund schemes structured around a specific maturity year with a dynamic glide-path strategy that automatically shifts asset allocation from equity-heavy (high risk, high return) to debt-heavy (low risk, stable return) over time.
  • Structure: The asset allocation includes equity (Nifty LargeMidcap 250 Index), debt (government securities), gold and silver commodities, and arbitrage strategies, and the funds are treated as equity funds for taxation with long-term capital gains (LTCG) benefits, no lock-in, and a minimum investment of Rs.100.
  • Market: New Fund Offer (NFO) period runs from 19 June 2026 to 7 July 2026, and globally, target-date funds manage over USD 4 trillion in assets.

About BRICS (Brazil, Russia, India, China, and South Africa):
  • Origin: BRICS was formalised as BRIC in 2006 during the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA), bringing together Brazil, Russia, India, and China, and held its first summit in Yekaterinburg, Russia, in 2009.South Africa joined in September 2010, transforming BRIC into BRICS.
  • Expansion: Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, and the United Arab Emirates (UAE) joined BRICS as full members in 2024, followed by Indonesia in 2025, expanding the grouping to ten member countries.
  • 2026 Chairship: India assumed the BRICS Chairmanship on 1 January 2026, marking its fourth presidency after 2012, 2016, and 2021.

11.16  India Becomes World’s Top Ship Recycling Nation in 2025 with 35.4% Global Sharep.205
Exam Hints:
  • What: India becomes world’s top ship recycling nation in 2025
  • Announced by: MoPSW
  • Report: Released by UNCTAD
  • Achievement: MIV 2030 target achieved 5 years early
  • Global Share: 35.4% in 2025 (volume – 2.99 million GT), 30.1% in 2024 (1.86 million GT)
  • Hub: Alang-Sosiya Ship Recycling Yard handles ~97% of India’s ship recycling and is the world’s largest hub.
  • Financial Assistance: Rs.53.5 crore provided for modernisation; 115 facilities became HKC-compliant.
About India Ship Recycling Leadership 2025:
  • Scheme: Ship-breaking Credit Note Scheme (SbCN) offers credits worth 40% of scrap value (usable up to 5% of new vessel cost) along with Rs.53.5 crore modernization support enabling 115 HKC-compliant facilities.
  • Global: Baltic and International Maritime Council (BIMCO) projects over 16,000 vessels for recycling globally in the next decade, with India positioned to recycle 500–600 vessels annually and seeking inclusion under European Union Ship Recycling Regulations (EUSRR).
About Maritime India Vision (MIV) 2030:
  • Vision: MIV 2030 is a 10-year comprehensive maritime blueprint launched in 2021 by MoPSW, comprising 150+ initiatives across 10 themes to modernize ports, shipping, inland waterways, and logistics while superseding the Sagarmala initiative.
  • Finance: The plan envisions Rs.3,00,000–Rs.3,50,000 crore investment supported by the Maritime Development Fund (MDF) of Rs.25,000 crore, including Rs.2,500 crore central contribution over seven years for low-cost long-term financing.

16.16  IAF Receives Final Operational Clearance for Indigenous AEW&C System ‘Netra’p.281
Exam Hints:
  • What: Final operational clearance granted for Netra AEW&C
  • Who: IAF received from DRDO
  • Where: Bengaluru, Karnataka
  • Purpose: Enhance airborne surveillance, situational awareness, command & control, and battle management.
  • IOC Received: 2017
  • Lead Laboratory: Centre for Air Borne Systems, DRDO
  • Platform: Embraer EMB-145I aircraft
  • Radar: AESA radar with 240–300 km detection range.
  • Significance: India became the 5th country to develop an indigenous AEW&C capability.
About AEW&C system Netra:
  • Background: Netra programme was initiated in 2003 as a joint initiative of the IAF and the DRDO to develop an indigenous airborne surveillance system and reduce dependence on imported platforms.In 2004, the Government of India (GoI) sanctioned the project, with the Centre for Air Borne Systems (CABS) designated as the lead laboratory.IAF received Initial Operational Clearance (IOC) in 2017.
AEW&C Development:
  • Inception: India’s AEW&C journey begins with Project Guardian in 1983 and the maiden flight of HS-748 Avro Airborne Surveillance Platform (ASP) on November 5, 1990 marks a milestone in operational testing.
  • Induction: The program paused after the 1999 HS-748 Avro crash near Arakkonam, Tamil Nadu (TN), resumed in 2004, received IOC in 2015, and was inducted into the Indian Air Force in 2017, enhancing India’s surveillance and network-centric warfare capabilities.
About Indian Air Force (IAF):
  • Chief of Air Staff (CAS)- Air Chief Marshal Amar Preet Singh
  • Headquarters: New Delhi, Delhi
  • Established: 1932

  • Legal Status in India: In June 2022, the Supreme Court of India (SCI) recognised sex work as a profession, affirming that sex workers and their children are entitled to dignity and protection under Article 21 (Right to Life) of the Indian Constitution.Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act (ITPA), 1956, along with provisions in the Indian Penal Code (IPC) and Juvenile Justice Act (JJA), governs sex work and trafficking in India.

Background:

  • Trigger: The proclamation followed the Allahabad High Court verdict of 12 June 1975, which found Indira Gandhi guilty of electoral malpractices, annulled her 1971 election, and barred her from holding elected office.
  • Observance: The first official observance of Samvidhaan Hatya Diwas was held on 25 June 2024.

  • Targets: It seeks to establish 5 Million Metric Tonnes (MMT) of annual Green Hydrogen production capacity supported by 125 Gigawatts (GW) of dedicated renewable energy capacity, attract investments exceeding Rs.8 lakh crore, generate over 6 lakh employment opportunities, and reduce annual CO₂ emissions by approximately 50 million tonnes (MT).

22.1  New Species Mesalina bishnoi Discovered in Rajasthan; First Record of Genus Mesalina in Indiap.392
Exam Hints:
  • What: Discovery of new lizard species Mesalina bishnoi
  • By whom: ZSI
  • Where: Near Gajner, Bikaner district, Rajasthan
  • Significance: Named after Bishnoi community
  • Objective: First specimen-based evidence of genus Mesalina in India
Background:
  • The species belongs to the arid-adapted lacertid lizards and was named in honour of the Bishnoi community for its conservation ethos.
About the Discovery of Mesalina bishnoi:
  • Overview: Mesalina bishnoi is a newly described small, fast-moving, diurnal lizard (snout-vent length ~39.2 millimeter, mm) discovered in the Thar biogeographic province of Rajasthan.
  • Identification: The species shows greyish to olive-brown coloration with dorsolateral stripes from neck to tail, black markings behind the eyes, and a white-spotted mottled camouflage pattern, belonging to the family Lacertidae.
  • Methodology: Its identification was confirmed through morphological examination and mitochondrial DNA (Deoxyribonucleic Acid) analysis, establishing it as a distinct evolutionary lineage within the Mesalina watsonana species complex.

22.2  Scientists Discovered New Lynx Spider Species Hamataliwa mawlyngot in Meghalayap.392
Exam Hints:
  • What: Discovery of a new lynx spider species, Hamataliwa mawlyngot
  • By whom: ZSI and the University of Calcutta
  • Where: Mawlyngot village, East Khasi Hills, Meghalaya
  • Family: Belongs to family Oxyopidae (Lynx Spiders)
  • Publication: National Academy Science Letters.
  • Significance: First record of genus Hamataliwa in Meghalaya
Background:
  • The findings were published in the journal National Academy Science Letters.
About Hamataliwa mawlyngot:
  • Overview: It belongs to the family Oxyopidae, found inhabiting dense vegetation on Molucca brambles along the biodiverse hillside slopes of Mawlyngot, known for its tea plantations.
  • Characteristics: The species is an extremely small lynx spider, smaller than a fingernail, that hunts prey using speed, agility, and sharp vision rather than constructing webs.
  • Ecological Role: As a predator of insects, the species contributes to ecosystem balance and serves as a natural biological control agent that may help reduce agricultural pest populations.
  • Significance of the Discovery: The study, authored by Souvik Sen, Upasana Bhattacharya, and Puthoor Pattammal Sudhin, expands the known distribution of the lynx spider genus Hamataliwa beyond its earlier records from southern India, China, and Southeast Asia, helping bridge a key geographical gap in its range.

22.3  ATREE Scientists Discover Two New Microscopic Snail Species in Meghalaya’s Limestone Cavesp.393
Exam Hints:
  • What: Discovery of two new microscopic snail species
  • Species: Georissa meghalayaensis and Acmella bensoni
  • Where: Krem Puri and Arwah limestone caves, Meghalaya
  • Publisher: European Journal of Taxonomy
  • Features: Georissa meghalayaensis – orangish-red shell, mesh-like ridgesAcmella bensoni – translucent whitish shell, fine densely packed ribs
Background:
  • The findings were published in the European Journal of Taxonomy, reporting the discovery of the two species in Meghalaya, part of the Indo-Burma Biodiversity Hotspot with around 1,200 limestone caves.
About Meghalaya Micro-Snail Discovery:
  • Species: Georissa meghalayaensis, endemic to Meghalaya, was discovered near the entrance of Krem Puri cave and has an orangish-red shell with intricate mesh-like ridges, while Acmella bensoni, named after William H. Benson, was found deeper inside Krem Puri and Arwah caves with a translucent whitish shell featuring deep grooves and densely packed ribs.
  • Features: Both species are extremely small, vividly coloured snails adapted to limestone cave habitats and require microscopic examination for identification, with related regional records from Manipur and Mizoram.
  • Threats: Their habitats face threats from heavy tourist footfall, artificial lighting, cave stairway construction, limestone mining, and habitat alteration.
